pages.text: The whole can be an amount, like 32 A. For 3/4 of it, cut it into 4 equal pieces of 8 A. Three of them make 24 A.

pages.why: The bottom number, 4, cuts the 20 into four equal pieces. 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so each piece is 5.

pages.name: Three quarters of 20
pages.task: Each quarter of 20 is 5. Colour 3/4 of the bar, then find 3/4 of 20.
pages.why: The top number, 3, takes three of the quarters. Each is 5, so 3 × 5 = 15.

pages.task: A 100 m drum has had 3/10 of its cable used. How much is left?
pages.why: One tenth of 100 m is 10 m, so 30 m was used. That leaves 100 − 30 = 70 m, the seven tenths still on the drum.

pages.task: How many minutes is 2/3 of an hour?
pages.why: An hour is 60 minutes, so one third is 60 ÷ 3 = 20 minutes. Two thirds are 2 × 20 = 40 minutes.

pages.name: Which is more?
pages.task: Which is more, 2/3 of 30 m or 3/4 of 24 m?
pages.why: 2/3 of 30 m is 20 m, and 3/4 of 24 m is 18 m. The bigger fraction is of a smaller amount, so here it gives less.
